CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old female presents with left shoulder pain lasting one week. Pain began during gymnastics class when patient fell into an awkward position during a move. Patient reports pain with any movement of the left shoulder. Patient attempted self-treatment with Tylenol for 2-3 days without relief. X-ray shows no fractures or broken bones; findings are consistent with joint injury.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Past surgery on left arm.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (acetaminophen) - taken for 2-3 days without relief.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in gymnastics class.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Left shoulder demonstrates pain with movement, including pain with upward and backward movements. Patient reports any movement of the left shoulder causes pain.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fractures or broken bones identified. Findings consistent with joint injury.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left shoulder joint injury from gymnastics trauma. Plan: Ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week. May use ice or heat pad for pain relief. Rest left arm while healing. Avoid carrying heavy weights with left arm for 3-4 weeks; use right hand instead. Follow-up in 3 weeks to reassess. Consider repeat x-ray at follow-up if pain persists. Alternative options include Advil or Aleve.
